full_judgment:
Mr. Abu Taher Md. Saifur Rahman, J:-This Rule relates to an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act preferred by the pre-emptor petitioner seeking condonation of delay of 500 days towards preferring an Civil Revision against Judgment and order dated 01.12.2009 passed by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Naogaon in Miscellaneous Appeal No.85 of 2007 allowing the same and thereby affirming the Judgment and Order dated 16.08.2007 passed by the Eleventh Court of Assistant Judge, Naogaon in Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2001 rejected the Miscellaneous Case. 

 2. Mr. S.N. Goswami, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the appellate Court below passed the impugned judgment and order dated 01.12.2009. The pre-emptor petitioner filed an application for certified copy of the said judgment on 01.12.2009 and it was ready for delivery on 07.01.2010. The petitioner obtained the certified copy on the same day i.e. on 07.01.2010. Thereafter he came to Dhaka and appointed the learned Advocate on 20.02.2010 for filing the civil revisional application before this Court. After received the certified copy of the impugned judgment the learned Advocate advised the petitioners' tadbirkar to come with all depositions of the witnesses along with written objection. Due to jaundice, the tadbirkar of the petitioner fall in sick and recovered on 28.09.2010. Thereafter he came to Dhaka on 02.10.2010 but on the way of his journey he was attacked by some miscreants in bus and found senseless position in Dhaka Medical College Hospital. After recovery he came to his own village. On 19.08.2011 the petitioner came to know that his tadbirkar failed to handover the relevant papers to his concerned lawyer. Thereafter the petitioner himself came to Dhaka on 20.08.2011 and handed over the relevant papers to his lawyer on 22.08.2011. After received the all relevant papers, the concerned lawyer prepared and filed the revisional application before this Court. By this time the statutory period of limitation for preferring a Civil Revision has expired. In the entire process a delay of 500 days has taken place which was quite unintentional. 

 5. I have perused the application for condonation of delay filed by the petitioner. On perusal of the said application it appears that the petitioner could not explained the cause of delay in his application properly. The learned Advocate for the petitioner contended that though the petitioner could not explained the cause of delay properly but there is a serious complicated legal questioned is involved which need to be disposed of on merits. In support of his contention he pointed out that this is a pre-emption case. The pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance in the suit jote. But both the Courts below committed an error of law in not considering the facts that the deed in question is completely out and out sale deed as per Hindu Dayabhaga Law. 

 8. On perusal of the subject matter of the suit it appears to me that there is a complicated legal matters are involved which should be disposed of on merits. Thus in the above facts and circumstances of the case and the reason as stated above I found substance in the application filed by the petitioner under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
